thread:
PagerDuty Bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT triggered — inference p99 latency breach on prod (region-us-east). Alert: initial spike at 20:17 UTC, sustained for ~6m. Paging Sam (oncall).
Sam: on it. can someone grab SLO impact? p95 vs p99 numbers?
Maya: seeing p95 ~220ms -> normal, p99 ~2.1s and tail at 6-8s for streaming requests. Lots of streaming stalls flagged. Investigating auth/config fetch paths.
Adele: confirm increased 5xxs in gateway logs where config-fetch returns 504 from config-store. Also auth token store had elevated latencies. Correlating with DB slow queries.
Sam: thx. tagging product teams. @Rian any customer-facing alerts to send?
Rian: pinging comms after we know scope. Do we have affected customers list from gateway logs? if streaming stalls = possible UX impact for several customers.
Maya: running a quick query to map requests hitting inference path -> control-plane dependencies. Command:

```
kubectl logs -l app=inference-gateway -n prod --since=10m | jq '. | select(.route=="/stream") | {ts, user_id, status, latency_ms, err}' | head -n 200
```

Maya: sample shows auth backend rtt spiking to 1.8s for ~30% of requests, config-fetch 504s at 20:18. rate-limit service backoff seen in traces.
Adele: here's a trace dump snippet:

```
[trace-id=abc123] gateway -> auth (t=1800ms) -> token-store -> db (t=1400ms) => fallback missing -> gateway stalls streaming
```

Sam: root cause hypothesis: DB/Control-plane saturation causing auth/config slowness; inference runtime waiting on control-plane (blocking feature flag/config fetch) causing streaming tail latency.
Maya: rolling temporary mitigations:
- enable local config cache (TTL=60s) on gateway
- widen auth cache window (allow cached tokens for +30s)
- route streaming to dedicated inference pool with cached routes if possible

Adele: I can patch gateway config for local cache. deploying quick patch to canary now.
DeployBot: deploy started for gateway/cache-hotfix -> canary pods (2) -> logs: ready.
Maya: canary looks good, reducing auth calls by ~70% for canary traffic. Promoting to 20%.
Sam: promoting to 50% then 100% if metrics hold. also bumping rate-limit token bucket temporarily to avoid rejecting legitimate traffic.
Adele: command applied:

```
curl -XPOST "https://ops-api.prod/configs/gateway/cache" -d '{"local_ttl":60, "stale_while_revalidate":30}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_API"
```

Maya: metrics after canary promote: p99 down from 2.1s -> 480ms, streaming tail improved to sub-1s for 95% traffic. Some DB-backed auth calls still slow for minority of requests.
Sam: good improvement. keeping on-call until stable. Sam -> handoff note for next oncall: monitor p99 <700ms and streaming error rate <0.5% for 15m.
Rian: customer impact assessment: looks like 6 customers had intermittent streaming stalls (<= 10 minutes each). No data loss. Recommend status page "degraded performance" for affected customers if we exceed 30m.
Maya: additional diagnostics: running slow query log for token-store DB now. suspect index regression on token lookup after yesterday's migration.
Adele: checking last schema migration & slow queries. If index regression, we can rollback migration or add index quick.
Maya: slow query sample:

```
SELECT * FROM tokens WHERE user_id = $1 AND revoked = false;
-- 95th: 5ms, 99th: 1.4s, full scan noted on explain
```

Adele: adding index on (user_id, revoked) as fast rollbackable migration. Applying to replica first.
Sam: proceed, but watch locks. If it causes table locks, stop and fallback to app-side caching.
Adele: running on replica -> no locks. schedule on primary at low traffic window (in 10m); will monitor.
DeployBot: migration job started on primary -> row-level locks minimal -> complete.
Maya: token lookup p99 back to 25ms on metrics. auth latencies back to baseline.
Sam: great. follow-up actions:
- Adele to open rollback/patch PR for gateway cache (short-term config) -> DONE
- Maya to add alert for token-store query plan change -> TODO
- Ops to run postmortem if SLO breach lasted >30m -> Sam to lead
Rian: I'll draft a short customer note saying we mitigated and latency restored, monitoring continuing.
Sam: handing off to Maya for overnight watch. Handoff summary posted below.

Maya: HANDOFF: monitoring p99<700ms, streaming errors <0.5%, token-store query plan stable. Pager on for 4h. If p99>1s for >5m escalate to eng-runtime.
Sam: thanks. closing active paging. :thumbsup:
PagerDuty Bot: Incident resolved (brief SLO breach) — duration 18m. Tags: auth, config-fetch, db-indexing, streaming-tail.
